problem: Self-training open-vocabulary detectors that use image-level weak supervision produce noisy, base-class-biased pseudo boxes that hurt novel-class detection. Topological maps for visual navigation typically use whole images as nodes, which gives coarse granularity and weak connectivity.
motivation: Open-vocabulary detection lets a robot recognize arbitrary landmarks without class-specific supervision, which is needed for semantically meaningful navigation. Topological maps are cheaper than metric maps, but they need finer object-level structure and reliable semantics to be useful.
key_idea: Debias pseudo-box self-training with a curriculum (progressive filtering plus adaptive class-aware/class-agnostic selection), then use the resulting open-vocabulary detector to build an object-level topological map from image segments and plan over it with semantic differences between nodes.
insight: The abstract states that the detector's bias toward base classes is strongest early in training, so mismatched detections are removed early and class-aware labeling is favored later as novel-class ability grows. It reports that this simple curriculum improves detection on several benchmarks without complex mechanisms. No ablation detail is available from the abstract alone.
method: Progressive Pseudo-label Filtering (PPF): removes mismatched detections early in training, when the detector's base-class bias is highest.
Adaptive Pseudo-label Selection (APS): merges class-aware and class-agnostic pseudo-labeling, giving class-aware labels more weight as novel-class detection matures.
Debiased Curriculum Self-Training (DCS): the overall self-training framework that combines PPF and APS to train an open-vocabulary detector.
Object-level topological map: builds nodes from image segments rather than whole images, giving finer granularity and better interconnectivity.
Semantic map augmentation: uses the DCS detector to add semantic labels to nodes so the agent can rely on more dependable landmarks.
Semantic-difference planning: a planning strategy that takes the semantic difference between nodes into account.

setting.backbone: open-vocabulary detector trained with DCS (specific architecture not given in the abstract)
setting.training_data: detection data for base classes plus image-level weak supervision for pseudo boxes (details not given in the abstract)
setting.observation: visual (RGB) observations; not detailed in the abstract

results: The abstract claims DCS markedly improves detection performance across multiple open-vocabulary benchmarks. It also reports superior navigation outcomes in a simulator with the object-level topological map. No numbers or named baselines are given.
limitations: Navigation is evaluated only in simulation and only for static settings; dynamic environments are left to future work.
The abstract gives no quantitative results, so the size of the gains cannot be assessed.
